key_insight: MedRLM proposes a recursive, multimodal framework that repeatedly inspects and verifies long, heterogeneous patient data instead of relying on a single prompt or retrieval step.
clinical_relevance: It is designed to support auditable clinical decision-making across longitudinal records, imaging, sensor data, and referral pathways, especially when cases are complex or high-risk.
method: Coordinates specialized agents for EHR text, medical images, sensor streams, guideline retrieval, uncertainty auditing, and referral planning.
Builds a Clinical Evidence Graph Memory to link patient observations with retrieved evidence, biomarkers, definitions, and referral criteria.
Uses sensor-triggered recursion and uncertainty gating to deepen reasoning when abnormal patterns or low-confidence cases appear.
evidence_signal: The abstract describes a planned evaluation using public and credentialed datasets spanning EHR, radiology, ECG, ICU time series, and referral-proxy outcomes.
watch_item: The framework’s real-world usefulness will depend on reliable data integration, calibration of uncertainty, and careful clinician oversight in high-stakes settings.
paper_title: MedRLM: Recursive Multimodal Health Intelligence for Long-Context Clinical Reasoning, Sensor-Guided Screening, Evidence-Grounded Decision Support, and Community-to-Tertiary Referral Optimization
